description: The organization's audit trail — the answer to "what changed on this item?", "what did somebody do last week?", "who moved this and when?". Newest first, one merged feed over item, ticket and order events: assignments, moves, status and category changes, renames, quantity adjustments and stock moves, pack/unpack, code attach/detach, custom-field edits, ticket transitions and checklist results, order transitions. Narrow it with `itemId` (that one item's history), `actorUserId` (one person — ids come from list_members), `sources` (["items"], ["tickets"], ["orders"]) and a date window: pass `since` / `until` as calendar days ("2026-08-01"), `until` included. This server has no timezone and does no conversion, so a bare day is the safe form; the legacy `dateFrom` / `dateTo` epochs still work, pass exactly one of each pair. Each row is one flat sentence: `atIso` when, `actorName` who (`viaAgent: true` = they did it through an AI agent), `type` what happened, `subject` what it happened to, `field` which attribute — the org's own label for a custom field — and `from` / `to` the two ends of the change, with `amount` where a number moved. Give your user the row's `webUrl`, not the ids: those are machine handles for your follow-up calls. A row marked `featureLocked: true` belongs to a module this organization's plan does not include (maintenance, orders) — it is kept because history is a record, but it carries NO `webUrl` and there is nothing to open: say that this activity sits in a module their plan does not cover, rather than offering a link or claiming the record is missing. Ask for `limit` 20 (default, max 50) and page with `nextCursor` rather than pulling a big window at once — the trail can be long. A filtered page can come back EMPTY while `isDone` is false: the filters run after the page is cut, so an empty page means "nothing matched HERE", not "nothing left" — keep paging with `nextCursor` until `isDone` is true before telling your user there is no history. Requires the manager role: the org-wide trail is an admin surface, so tell a plain member to ask a manager instead of retrying.

actorUserId.description: Only this person's actions — the userId from list_members

cursor.description: The `nextCursor` from a previous call — pages further back in time

dateFrom.description: Lower bound as epoch milliseconds. Prefer `since` — pass exactly one of the two

dateTo.description: Upper bound as epoch milliseconds. Prefer `until` — pass exactly one of the two

since.description: Only events from this calendar day onward, "YYYY-MM-DD". Prefer this over dateFrom — a bare day has no timezone to get wrong, and this server does none of that conversion for you

sources.description: Which records to read events from; omit for all three

types.description: Only these ITEM event types — e.g. ["assigned", "moved", "status_changed", "quantity_adjusted", "custom_field_changed"]. An unknown value returns an error naming the whole valid set. Does not filter ticket or order rows

until.description: Only events up to and INCLUDING this calendar day, "YYYY-MM-DD". Prefer this over dateTo

name: list_activity

amount.description: How many moved — stock moves and order lines

atIso.description: When it happened, ISO-8601 UTC timestamp — read THIS one; the server does no timezone conversion

featureLocked.description: Present and true when this event belongs to a module the organization's plan does not include (e.g. maintenance or orders). The row is shown because history is a record, but it carries NO webUrl — tell the user this activity is in a module their plan does not include rather than offering to open it. Absent = a normal row

field.description: Which attribute changed — the organization's own label for a custom field, the checklist line for a ticket check, the item name on an order line

from.description: The value before, already rendered: a name, a status, a number, or a calendar day. Absent when there was none

kind.description: Which record the event belongs to: "item", "ticket" or "order"

note.description: The note the actor left, when any

subject.description: What it happened to: the item or model name, the ticket title, or the order's request text. "—" when the record has since been deleted (the row is kept — an audit trail must not lie by omission)

to.description: The value after, same rendering. Absent when it was cleared

type.description: What happened: assigned | moved | status_changed | renamed | category_changed | quantity_adjusted | stock_moved | contained | removed | code_attached | custom_field_changed | ticket and order transitions | …

viaAgent.description: Present and true when they did it through an AI agent. Absent = they did it themselves in the app

webUrl.description: Link to the record in the web app — give your user THIS, never the raw ids. Absent on featureLocked rows, which have nowhere to link to

isDone.description: True = this was the last page; there is nothing older to fetch. An EMPTY `events` array while this is false is normal on a filtered read — the filters are applied after the page is cut, so that page simply held no matching rows: keep paging with `nextCursor` instead of concluding there is no history

nextCursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page further back in time. Present only while isDone is false

title: List activity
